about: Stacked claims (coordinator, Part 16; classify.mjs offSiteVerdicts `stacked`, matrix.mjs judge): a violation on a line where Solid's first throw halted the run before the rule's own code could fire. A violation means "wrong if it runs", so such a row is no false positive by itself, but the halt is no evidence either: a (first code, rule) pair scores `stacked-claim` only when a pattern here, with the first throw removed and the rule's condition kept, makes Chrome report a code of the rule. Every pair's patterns are checked on each patterns run (patterns.mjs `stackedProblems`): each must be judged fine with a code of the rule. A `repeat` pair (`kind`) is the rule's own code reported once, off the violation's lines: Solid reports some codes once, so its twin removes that first report. A pair not listed scores false-positive.

CLEANUP_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE|missing-owner.why: a helper an owned tracked scope and an ownerless caller both run: with the tracked caller gone, the ownerless call reports NO_OWNER_CLEANUP

PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE|sync-comput.why: createMemo(async, { sync: true }) where creating is allowed: SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC

PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK|sync-comput.why: as above, out of the effect callback

PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK|missing-own.why: an effect's apply callback has no owner: an owner-needing call that creates no primitive there reports NO_OWNER_CONTEXT and NO_OWNER_CLEANUP

NO_OWNER_CONTEXT|missing-context-provide.why: useContext with an owner and no provider: CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND

MISSING_EFFECT_FN|leaf-owner-forbidden-c.why: the createEffect given its effect function, in an action onSettled runs: PRIMITIVE_IN_FORBIDDEN_SCOPE

ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE|flush-in-ac.why: the action run from a handler, with no owned scope to throw first: flush inside it rejects with FLUSH_IN_ACTION. With `act()` in a memo, ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE throws before the flush runs

UNTRACKED_READ_AFTER_AWAIT|reactive-read.why: Solid reports the read after an await once per compute: the census aw-helper-late helper reads before and after its own await and Chrome reports only the first; with that read gone, it reports the second (line 8)

STORE_WRITE_OUTSIDE_SETTER|no-store-muta.why: Solid reports the store write once: aw-shared-after-assign writes in the memo and in a helper after its await, Chrome reports the memo's; with that write gone, it reports the helper's (line 7)
